title: Hybrid Preemptible Ceiling and Device Affinity Orchestrator
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Implement an orchestrator that enforces per-tenant spend ceilings while preferring preemptible (spot) capacity and preserving SLOs by applying GPU-class affinity and graceful model-variant fallback policies.
background: Customers frequently hit cost spikes when the platform migrates work from spot to on-demand during market churn. Current routing picks cheapest available instance but lacks a tenant-level ceiling and device-class awareness. This leads to oscillations, disproportionate SLO violations for latency-sensitive tenants, and opaque billing impact. We need a coordinated policy that (1) exposes configurable budget caps, (2) prefers preemptible capacity where safe, and (3) binds requests to compatible GPU classes with explicit fallback degradation paths.
goals: Expose per-tenant daily and rolling-30m spend ceilings that can be enforced at request admission.
Route preferring preemptible instances up to a hedging threshold while keeping a reserved on-demand fallback budget for latency-critical traffic.
Introduce GPU-class affinity hints in routing decisions (e.g., A100-80GB, H100, T4) and document compatibility matrix for model variants.
Implement a deterministic, graded fallback sequence that degrades model variant or precision (fp16 -> int8 quantized variant -> smaller model) rather than abrupt request rejection.
Ship observability: per-tenant spend burn-rate, hedged vs fallback counts, preemptible eviction rate, and effective latency/SLO delta.
Provide a clear operator override for emergency reserve capacity to protect high-SLA customers.
non_goals: We will not change global pricing or billing primitives in this ticket; integrations with billing will be read-only counters for now.
This work will not add new physical GPU types to our fleet—it only uses existing instance classes and model build variants.
We will not implement long-horizon predictive market bidding in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Config schema that accepts daily and rolling budget caps per tenant and per-route in console and API (validated by unit tests).
Routing layer honors budget caps: when a tenant hits caps, low-priority routes should be routed to degraded variants or rate-limited, high-priority routes should consume emergency reserve if flagged.

Hedging: system uses preemptible instances until eviction signal rate exceeds threshold OR spend burn rate would exceed cap in next 30 minutes, then stepwise move to on-demand using device affinity rules.
Fallback chain implemented and exercised in integration tests: primary model -> quantized variant -> small-model fallback -> 503 only if all fallbacks exhausted and route priority == low.
Dashboard panels show per-tenant spend vs cap, hedged preemptible volume, fallback counts, and 95th/99th latency delta with comparisons to baseline.
Chaos test: simulate spot eviction burst in staging and demonstrate graceful degradation with <=10% increase in 99th latency for high-priority tenants and no unhandled errors.
Operator override API to consume emergency reserve (audit-logged) works and documented in runbook.
design_notes: Policy engine will live in routing-service as an independent component that receives admission requests with tenant, route, priority, model, and hints (sequence length, cache hit probability).

Budget store: use existing tenant-usage-timeseries with a fast in-memory cache + periodic reconciliation with billing counters. Budget enforcement will be eventual-consistent with conservative slow-path checks on admission to avoid overspend.

Device affinity: introduce GPU_class hint on model metadata. Routing will prefer exact class matches; if unavailable, consult compatibility matrix to choose next-best class with adjusted latency multiplier.

Fallbacks expressed as an ordered list in model config: [primary_variant, quantized_variant, small_variant, degrade_to_cached]. Each fallback has an expected token-cost multiplier and SLO impact estimate.

Hedging algorithm: maintain 'preemptible_util' per-tenant. Preemptible route accepted if preemptible_util + estimated_cost <= cap * preemptible_share. If eviction rate rises above eviction_threshold, increase preemptible_util multiplier to force migration to on-demand for critical routes.
Operator override stores consumption in a reserved bucket with audit entries and time-limited TTL.
implementation_plan: Add budget schema to admin API and Console: UI controls for daily and rolling caps, emergency reserve toggle.
Extend model metadata to include gpu_class and fallback_chain; add compatibility matrix in model catalog service.

Routing-service: implement policy engine with admission checks, device-affinity chooser, and fallback executor that rewrites request to variant or responds with route-specific rate-limit when necessary.
Runtime integration: ensure KV cache and batching preserve semantics when falling back to smaller models (prefix cache compatibility rules documented).
Add integration tests that exercise eviction scenarios, cap exhaustion, and operator override behavior.
Create dashboard in Console: per-tenant spend, hedged vs fallback breakdown, eviction heatmap; add alerts for >75% cap burn rate over 30m and >5% fallback rate sustained over 10m.
Roll out to internal canary tenants, observe metrics for 72h, then soft launch to 5% of production tenants with highest cost volatility.
Runbook: document steps to diagnose cap-related rejections, to manually adjust preemptible_share, and to perform emergency reserve consumption.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Budget enforcement latency could allow short-term overspend. Mitigation: pessimistic slow-path that rejects admissions if cache stale and estimated cost would exceed cap; reconcile regularly and notify customers on near-cap events.

Risk: Fallback compatibility breaks structured output or function-calling. Mitigation: add variant compatibility flags; disallow fallback for routes that require strict contract until explicit opt-in.
Risk: Increased orchestration complexity could add latency. Mitigation: micro-benchmark policy engine and keep admission path <2ms p50; offload heavy checks to async validators when possible.
Risk: Operator override abused. Mitigation: require two-person approval for overrides >$X and audit logs exported to SIEM.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy feature-flagged policy engine behind routing-service flag; test with synthetic load and simulated cloud preemptions.
Phase 2 (internal): enable for internal tenants and platform team customers; gather telemetry for 72h; iterate on thresholds.
Phase 3 (canary): 5% production tenants with automated rollback on cap-breach or SLO regression.
Phase 4 (general): enable by default with opt-out for tenants needing custom handling; provide migration docs and support runbook.
Emergency: operator override documented and accessible via Console with audit trail and TTL.
monitoring_and_slos: Per-tenant burn-rate vs cap (real-time), alerts at 60%/80%/95% of cap for 30m sustained.
Preemptible eviction rate per-region, per-GPU-class. Alert when eviction_rate > 2% over 5m for a device class.
Fallback rate per-route and per-tenant; target <=3% for high-priority routes.
Admission latency for policy engine p50 < 2ms, p99 < 15ms.
SLO delta: 95th and 99th latency delta vs baseline for high-priority tenants: target <10% increase after fallback.
Audit log trail for operator overrides and manual reserve consumption.
